**h01** — S3 presign refresh runner — every 12 hours (plus one immediate pass at boot) — wired in `startBackgroundRunners`

- Component: `s3presign.Runner` (`server/runner/s3presign/runner.go:17`), work done in `CheckAndPresign` (`server/runner/s3presign/runner.go:47`) — re-presigns S3 attachment URLs whose `LastPresignedTime` is older than 4 days (URLs expire at 5 days).
- Schedule: `runnerInterval = 12h` ticker (`server/runner/s3presign/runner.go:27`, `:29-41`).
- Wiring: `server/server.go:162` (construct), `server/server.go:163` (immediate `RunOnce`), `server/server.go:166-171` (goroutine `Run`), called from `Server.Start` at `server/server.go:129`.

**h02** — delivery function: `webhook.Post` — `internal/webhook/webhook.go:120` (HTTP POST issued at `:152`); async enqueue via `webhook.PostAsync` `internal/webhook/webhook.go:184` + 4 queue workers `internal/webhook/webhook.go:42-55`.
Protection: two layers —
- Dial-time SSRF guard: `safeClient` with `safeDialContext` (`internal/webhook/webhook.go:32-37`, `:59-77`) resolves the host and refuses reserved/private IPs, which also defeats DNS rebinding. Ranges in `reservedCIDRs` / `isReservedIP` — `internal/webhook/validate.go:14-23`, `:44-54` (loopback, RFC-1918, 169.254.0.0/16 incl. cloud IMDS, IPv6 equivalents).
- Config-time validation: `webhook.ValidateURL` (`internal/webhook/validate.go:62`) called when a user creates/updates a webhook (`server/router/api/v1/user_service_webhooks.go:74`, `:161`, `:182`).
- Escape hatch: `webhook.AllowPrivateIPs` (`internal/webhook/validate.go:41`), set from the `--allow-private-webhooks` flag at `cmd/memos/main.go:49`.

**h03** — abstraction package: `github.com/usememos/memos/internal/idp` (`internal/idp/idp.go:1`, defines `IdentityProviderUserInfo`); implementation package: `github.com/usememos/memos/internal/idp/oauth2` (`internal/idp/oauth2/oauth2.go`, `IdentityProvider` + `NewIdentityProvider` at `:19`/`:27`). OAuth2 is the only concrete protocol shipped.

**h04** — no.
Evidence: `mysql.NewDB` is declared once (`store/db/mysql/mysql.go:20`) and the package `store/db/mysql` is imported at exactly one place in the repo — `store/db/db.go:8`, used only in the `case "mysql"` branch of `NewDBDriver` (`store/db/db.go:22`). A repo-wide grep for `store/db/mysql` returns that single import line. (Tests go through `db.NewDBDriver` too — `store/test/store.go:28`, `:50`. Other `mysql.` references are the third-party `go-sql-driver/mysql` and `testcontainers-go/modules/mysql` packages, not this driver.)

**h05** — explicit Go code, per driver, inside the delete-user transaction. There is no DB-level cascade.
- Explicit deletes: `deleteReactionsByCreatorTx` (reactions the user made) and `deleteReactionsByContentIDsTx` (reactions on the user's memos and their comment subtree), invoked from `deleteUserTargetsTx` — `store/db/sqlite/user_delete.go:96` and `:102` (declarations at `:380` and `:400`); mirrored in `store/db/postgres/user_delete.go` and `store/db/mysql/user_delete.go`. Entry point `DB.DeleteUser` `store/db/sqlite/user_delete.go:29`, reached via `Store.DeleteUser` `store/user.go:171-172`.
- Checked for a DB rule and found none: the `reaction` table has no foreign key or `ON DELETE` clause in any dialect — `store/migration/sqlite/LATEST.sql:92-99`, `store/migration/postgres/LATEST.sql:91-98`, `store/migration/mysql/LATEST.sql:91-98`. The only `FOREIGN KEY ... ON DELETE CASCADE` in the schemas is on `memo_share.memo_id` (`store/migration/sqlite/LATEST.sql:109` and dialect equivalents).

- `UpdateMemo` — `server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:401` (dispatch at `:513`)

Convergence: all paths funnel through `webhook.PostAsync` (`internal/webhook/webhook.go:184`) into the single delivery function `webhook.Post` — `internal/webhook/webhook.go:120`.

**h10** — `(*filter.Engine).CompileToStatement` — `internal/filter/engine.go:74` — approx. 37 call sites (graph fan-in 36), the highest of anything declared under `internal/`.
Runners-up: `filter.NewEngine` `internal/filter/engine.go:24` (~32) and `filter.NewSchema` `internal/filter/schema.go:89` (~29).

**h11** — counting packages *outside* `store/` (i.e. excluding `store/db/*` and `store/test`):
- 1st: `store.User` — 7 packages (`server/auth`, `server/notification`, `server/router/api/v1`, `server/router/api/v1/test`, `server/router/fileserver`, `server/router/frontend`, `server/router/rss`), ~36 files repo-wide (`store/user.go:38`)

**h12** — concrete method: `(*sqlite.DB).CreateMemo` — `store/db/sqlite/memo.go:16` (the `INSERT INTO \`memo\` ...` statement is built at `:40-41` and executed at `:42`).
Determination: the driver is chosen at runtime from `profile.Driver`, whose default is `"sqlite"` — `cmd/memos/main.go:122` (`viper.SetDefault("driver", "sqlite")`) and `cmd/memos/main.go:130` (flag default). That profile feeds `db.NewDBDriver`, whose `switch profile.Driver` takes `case "sqlite": sqlite.NewDB(profile)` — `store/db/db.go:18-20`. The resulting value is stored as `Store.driver` (`store/store.go:48`), and `Store.CreateMemo` delegates straight to it — `store/memo.go:113` (`s.driver.CreateMemo`). So of the three `CreateMemo` implementations (sqlite/postgres/mysql), the sqlite one runs on a default install.

**r01** — Premise is wrong: there is no Redis anywhere in this codebase (no `redis` import in any `.go` file or in `go.mod`). The cache is a purpose-built in-process, in-memory cache: `store/cache/cache.go` (`Cache` struct at `:67`, `sync.Map`-backed, background `cleanupLoop` at `:83`). The store holds three instances — `instanceSettingCache`, `userCache`, `userSettingCache` — constructed in `store.New` at `store/store.go:51-53` with `cacheConfig{DefaultTTL: 10 * time.Minute, CleanupInterval: 5 * time.Minute, MaxItems: 1000}` (`store/store.go:40-45`). So user entries live **10 minutes**, keyed by user ID (`userCacheKey`, `store/user.go:88`), set on read/write paths (`store/user.go:98,122,132,143,167`) and explicitly invalidated on delete (`store/user_delete.go:40`). Entries can also be evicted early once the 1000-item cap is hit (`store/cache/cache.go:117-119`). Nothing is shared across processes.

**r02** — Premise is wrong: there is no per-user (or any) rate-limiting middleware in this codebase. No rate-limit package is imported (`golang.org/x/time/rate` and equivalents are absent from `go.mod`), and the only textual match for "rate limit" repo-wide is an aspirational comment in `internal/email/doc.go:86`. The Echo middleware stack is just `middleware.Recover()` and the CORS middleware (`server/server.go:51-52`); API auth is handled by `gatewayAuthMiddleware` / the Connect interceptor and `Authorizer.CheckAccess` (`server/router/api/v1/v1.go:67-90`), which do authn/authz only. The nearest thing to throttling is concurrency limiting, not request-rate limiting: weighted semaphores of 3 for thumbnails and 2 for image processing (`server/router/api/v1/v1.go:59-60`), a thumbnail semaphore in the file server (`server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:116`), a 256 MiB body cap (`server/router/api/v1/v1.go:20`), and a 128-slot webhook dispatch queue with 4 workers (`internal/webhook/webhook.go:39-55`).

**r03** — Premise is wrong: there is no nightly database-cleanup job, and no cron scheduler is running at all. `internal/scheduler` is a self-contained cron library (`internal/scheduler/scheduler.go`, `parser.go`, `middleware.go`), but it is imported only by its own tests — `internal/scheduler/example_test.go:10` and `internal/scheduler/integration_test.go:13`; no production file imports it, and `Scheduler.Register`/`Start` are never called outside tests. The `"0 2 * * *"` daily-cleanup expression that looks like the answer is only illustrative documentation in the package doc comment (`internal/scheduler/doc.go:16-22`). The only background work actually scheduled at runtime is the S3 presign runner on a 12-hour ticker (`server/server.go:162-171`, `server/runner/s3presign/runner.go:27`).

**r04** — Premise is wrong on both counts: neither NATS nor RabbitMQ is used, and there is no external broker or declared queue anywhere (`go.mod` contains no `nats`, `amqp`, `rabbitmq`, or `kafka` dependency). Webhook delivery is entirely in-process: an unbuffered-overflow-dropping Go channel `asyncPostQueue = make(chan *WebhookRequestPayload, 128)` (`internal/webhook/webhook.go:39`), drained by 4 goroutines started in `init()` (`internal/webhook/webhook.go:42-55`), each calling `webhook.Post` (`internal/webhook/webhook.go:120`). Producers call `webhook.PostAsync` (`internal/webhook/webhook.go:184`), which drops the payload with a warning when the channel is full (`:189-195`). There is no persistence, no retry, and no redelivery — an in-flight webhook is lost on restart.

**r05** — Premise is wrong: there is no GraphQL schema or GraphQL server in this codebase (zero matches for "graphql" in Go sources or `go.mod`). The public API is Protobuf/gRPC-defined, exposed over two HTTP transports plus several plain-HTTP routers:
- Service definitions: `proto/api/v1/*.proto` (`memo_service.proto`, `user_service.proto`, `auth_service.proto`, `attachment_service.proto`, `instance_service.proto`, `idp_service.proto`, `shortcut_service.proto`, `ai_service.proto`, `common.proto`), generated into `proto/gen/api/v1`.
- Transports: gRPC-Gateway REST mux and Connect RPC handlers, both registered in `(*APIV1Service).RegisterGateway` — `server/router/api/v1/v1.go:65` onward; Connect handlers in `server/router/api/v1/connect_services.go`.
- Additional surfaces: SSE hub (`server/router/api/v1/sse_hub.go`), HTTP file server at `/file/...` (`server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:121-125`), RSS (`server/router/rss/rss.go`), MCP (`server/router/mcp`, `server/server.go:92-96`), frontend static/sitemap (`server/router/frontend`), and `/healthz` (`server/server.go:67`).
